slides.title: Thailand Reading Scores, PISA, 2000-2022
slides.notes: Count up. Ask: What is this graph showing? Where is Thailand going?

slides.title: What is going wrong with reading around the world?
slides.body: Let's read and find out.
slides.notes: Today we learn to read deeply together. No one reads alone.

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• Reading well at 15 predicts your future success.
  • Thailand's scores keep falling, every year.
  • Reading is a skill you can learn — not a gift.
slides.notes: Frame in real-world outcomes. Reading is a life skill, not school only.

slides.title: A quick question
slides.body:
How many of you have read a book in Thai or English in the past 12 months?

Hand up. Look around.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Take a poll. Count hands. Do not judge. This is the problem we explore today.

slides.title: Watch the news report
slides.body:
Why is the Professor worried?

Why does he think reading ability is declining?
slides.notes: Two listening questions. Play the clip once. Let them watch, not write.
Play 0:00-2:37. Listen for the Harvard expert's worry and his reason.

slides.title: Time to read together
slides.body: Today we learn a way to read as a team.
slides.notes: We are going to read in groups of four. Each person has one special job.

slides.title: Task 1: How One Round Works
slides.body:
Each person in your group has one job.

You will change jobs for every reading chunk. There are four chunks.

The jobs are: Predictor, Clarifier, Questioner and Summariser.

The teacher will not talk or give you answers. Your job is to teach each other.
slides.notes: Four roles, four chunks. Each person does each role once. Teacher is silent.

slides.title: Task 2 · Before reading
slides.body:
PREDICTOR

Look at the heading. Guess what the section will say.

•The heading says… so I think this section will…
•I predict… because…
slides.notes: Only the Predictor speaks before reading. This is the first role.

slides.title: Task 2 · After reading
slides.body:
CLARIFIER
Say what was confusing. Fix it with your group.
QUESTIONER
Ask a genuine I wonder question, not a quick check.
SUMMARISER
Say the main idea of the chunk in one sentence.
slides.notes: Three roles speak, in turn, after reading. They build on each other.

slides.title: Task 3 · Read and Learn
slides.body:
Read the chunk on your worksheet. Watch for:

systematic review  ·  cognitive pull
slides.notes: This is the model chunk: What Is Going Wrong. Read silently. Do not speak.

slides.title: Task 4 · Model discussion
slides.body:
Listen to four students read one round.

Emma predicts · Jack clarifies · Sophie questions · Liam summarises
slides.notes: Play the model. Point to each role on the worksheet Task 4 as they speak.

slides.title: Task 5 · Discuss with your group
slides.body:
1Reading at 15 predicts your future.
2Reading pays at school and at work.
3Reading can be learned, not born.
4Thailand's fall is the sharpest.
slides.notes: Choose one question per chunk. Use the framework on the next slide.

slides.title: Give your opinion
slides.body:
OpinionIn my opinion… / I think…
Reasonbecause… / I think this because…
EvidenceThe text says… / In the article, it says…
DisagreeI'm not sure I agree… / I see it differently…
AgreeI agree, and also… / That's a good point, because…
ConclusionSo we agree that… / To sum up, we think…

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Six-step framework, on the worksheet too. The O-R-E line anchors it.

slides.title: Now you do it
slides.body: Read the whole reading pack together.
slides.notes: Groups of four. One role each. Rotate for each chunk.

slides.title: Work in your group of four
slides.body:
One role each.

For every chunk, rotate to a new role.

Everyone gets a turn at each role.
slides.notes: 4 chunks, 4 roles. Each person does each role once.

slides.title: The reading pack has four chunks
slides.body:
1Reading at 15 predicts your future
2Reading pays at school and at work
3Reading can be learned, not born
4Thailand's fall is the sharpest
slides.notes: Same four topics as Task 5. One chunk at a time.

slides.title: Your job, not the teacher's
slides.body:
Take notes as you read.

I will not speak or give answers.

You and your group manage it.
slides.notes: Emphasise: the teacher is silent. Students own the discussion.

slides.title: Silent reading
slides.body:
Read the chunk silently.

Take notes in your role.

Then start the discussion.
slides.notes: Timer auto-starts. Return to this slide for each chunk.

slides.title: Discuss the chunk
slides.body:
Clarify. Question. Summarise.

Then rotate roles.

Next chunk.
slides.notes: Timer auto-starts. Use the O-R-E framework.

slides.title: Open-class feedback
slides.body:
What surprised you in the readings?

What did your group learn?
slides.notes: Whole class. Elicit ideas about the problem and about reading together.

slides.title: The big discussion
slides.body: If we have time, we talk it out.
slides.notes: Only if time allows. Use the O-R-E framework.

slides.title: Final discussion
slides.body:
Say your opinion.

Give a reason.

Use an example from the text.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Timer auto-starts. One chunk question per group.
